answer: When an identity first requests write access, its request is held over an ember of probation: the newcomer must echo a fresh nonce through three independent relays before the inlet to the ledger opens. Two relays returning conflicting signatures, or a late echo, cuts the probationary thread short - every relay that forwarded the failed probe burns 8,000 POA of the candidate's bond on the spot. Each forged identity therefore costs the attacker a fresh 8,000 POA stake plus non-reusable relay fees, so the expense scales linearly with every fake account while honest verification stays free.
